item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission investigated risks involving confidential information at the Office of the Auditor General.
item.support: In view of the potential misconduct risk in the exposure of confidential information, the Commission commenced an investigation

item.text: The Commission found that inadequate access controls allowed two auditors to obtain private information about colleagues.
item.support: Two auditors, each a certified practicing accountant (CPA), had routinely accessed confidential information about other OAG officers

item.text: The Commission identified a risk from police names and addresses retained on a laptop after an audit, while finding no evidence that the information was shared.
item.support: There is no evidence the police data was shared with others.

item.text: The Commission formed an opinion of serious misconduct concerning an auditor's deliberate destruction of an encrypted storage device and its data.
item.support: In the circumstances, an opinion of serious misconduct is appropriate.

item.text: The Commission stressed that its misconduct opinion did not establish guilt of a criminal or disciplinary offence.
item.support: An opinion that serious misconduct has occurred is not, and is not to be taken as a finding or opinion

item.text: The Commission made five recommendations covering access restrictions, secure retention of audit data, internal checks and staff education.
item.support: The Commission recommends that public authorities ensure confidential material used for an audit by the OAG remains confidential at the conclusion of the audit.
